definitions.explanation: A name that identifies a person, including both given names and family names. Used especially in contexts discussing names as a category or system.

examples.japanese: {人名|じんめい}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}が{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: The reading of people's names is difficult.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{人名|じんめい}には{漢字|かんじ}が{使|つか}われることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Chinese characters are often used in Japanese personal names.

examples.japanese: {人名|じんめい}{用|よう}{漢字|かんじ}は{法律|ほうりつ}で{定|さだ}められている。
examples.english: The kanji permitted for use in personal names are determined by law.

notes:
Composed of {人|じん} (person) + {名|めい} (name). A formal, categorical term used when discussing names as a topic — in everyday conversation, {名前|なまえ} (name) is far more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人名|じんめい}{辞典|じてん} — dictionary of personal names
- {人名|じんめい}{用|よう}{漢字|かんじ} — kanji approved for use in names
- {人名|じんめい}{録|ろく} — name register; directory of people
- {人名|じんめい}の{由来|ゆらい} — origin of a person's name

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名前|なまえ} — name (everyday term; can refer to any name, not just people's)
- {氏名|しめい} — full name (formal; used on forms and documents)
- {姓名|せいめい} — family name and given name (formal pair)
- {人命|じんめい} — human life (same reading but different kanji and meaning)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {人名|じんめい}{用|よう}{漢字|かんじ} (name-use kanji) is a legally defined set of characters that can be used in given names. Parents must choose characters from this list or the {常用漢字|じょうようかんじ} when registering a child's name.
